sentences.text: The claimant is impugning the judgment and award dated 08.04.2010 passed in MVC.No.1386/2007 on the file of the Fast Track IV & M.A.C.T., Belgaum (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal'), awarding compensation of Rs.69,500/-, directing respondent Nos.1 and 2 to pay the same jointly and severally.
2. The parties are referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Brief facts of the case are that the claimant has filed the claim petition in M.V.C. N. 1386/2007 before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

It is stated that the claimant was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-22/U-5514 and in the meantime the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 22/X-8220 ridden his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle in which the claimant was proceeding, as a result of which the claimant sustained injuries, admitted to the hospital and was treated.
Claimant has suffered disability and spent huge amount towards his treatment.
4. It is contended that respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending motorcycle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the same, are liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, prays for allowing the claim petition.
5. Respondent No.1 has not contested the matter.
Respondent No.2 filed statement of objections denying the contentions taken by the claimant.
It is contended that the accident was only due to the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the claimant and therefore he is not entitled for compensation.
6. It is also contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective diving licence and therefore the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
Accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

7. On the basis of all these pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed;
"1.

Whether petitioner proves the accident occurred on 20.02.2007 at about 4.30 p.m. on Indal Over Bridge Circle near Service Road, Belgaum due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle KA-22/X8220 by its order?

Ajay Anupam S/O S N Pathak vs Shivanand A Hiremath on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194750155/
2 2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves his age, income, medical treatment and permanent disability?
3. Whether Respondent no.2 proves that it is not liable to pay the compensation as per the objections?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation and if so, from whom and what quantum?

5. To what decree or award?"
8.
The claimant examined himself as PW1, got examined PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P9 in support of his contentions.
Respondent No.2 has not lead any oral evidence but got marked Exs.R1 and R2 in support of its defence.

9. The Tribunal after taking into consideration all the materials on record, came to the conclusion that the claimant has contributed up to 50% in causing the accident and therefore apportioned the liability between the claimant and the rider of the offending motorcycle.
As a result, awarded compensation of Rs.69,500/- holding that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
10. Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred this appeal.

11. Heard Sri. Y.Lakshmikant Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri. K.Anandkumar, learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Smt. Anusha V.Sangavi for Sri. S.K.Kayakmath, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
12.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that even though the apportionment of liability was challenged by the claimant, now he is not pressing the said ground.

13. Learned counsel submitted that the claimant has suffered 2 fractures and the Doctor has given the disability certificate certifying that the claimant has suffered permanent partial disability up to 25%.
The Tribunal has not taken into consideration the income of the claimant and awarded the meager amount of compensation.
Therefore he prays for enhancing the compensation in the interest of justice.

14. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the appeal submitted that the Tribunal has taken into consideration the oral and documentary evidence and rightly awarded the compensation which is not unreasonable.
There are no grounds to enhance the compensation.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Perused the materials on record.
16.
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal requires interference of this Court?

My answer to the above point is partly in the affirmative for the following;
REASONS 17.
The factum of accident is not in dispute.
The insurer has not challenged the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate pertaining to the claimant.
As per this document, the claimant suffered fracture of left clavicle and fracture of left ulnar upper arm.
He was taken treatment as inpatient for 3 days and thereafter he was discharged.
The Tribunal has taken into consideration the income of the claimant at Rs.3,000/- per month.
The income of the claimant in the absence of any proof during 2007 could be taken at Rs.4,000/- per month by adopting the guildlines issued for settling the dispute before the Lok Adalath.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the said income could be taken into consideration for the claimant.

Since 50% of the liability is saddled on the claimant, his yearly income would be Rs.24,000/- (i.e., Rs.4,000 X 12 =
48,000 Less 50%).
18. Claimant was aged 34 years at the time of the accident.
Therefore the appropriate multiplier would be "16".

Taking into consideration the permanent physical disability at 15% to the whole body,
the claimant is entitled for loss of future income at Rs.57,600/- [i.e., Rs.24,000 X 16 [multiplier] X 15% [disability].
19.

Looking to the nature of injury i.e., 2 fractures sustained to the left clavicle and left ulnar upper arm, I am of the opinion that the claimant is entitled for compensation towards loss of income during laid up period for a period of three months at Rs.12,000/-[i.e., Rs.4,000 X 3 months].
The Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation on other heads and I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Hence I am of the opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs to be enhanced.

Since 50% of the liability is saddled on the claimant, the total compensation to be awarded to the claimant after deducting 50% is as under;
Sl. Heads Amount Amount No. (In (after  Rupees) deducting  50%)
1. Towards pain and sufferings 30,000/- 15,000/-
2. Towards loss of amenities 30,000/- 15,000/-
3. Towards medical expenses 16,000/- 8,000/-

4 . Towards special diet, 10,000/- 5,000/-
 conveyance and incidental  charges

5. Towards loss of income during 12,000/- 6,000/-
 laid up period 6.

Towards loss of future income  1,15,200/- 57,600/-
 TOTAL 1,06,600/-
 Amount awarded by the Tribunal 69,500/-
Ajay Anupam S/O S N Pathak vs Shivanand A Hiremath on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194750155/
4

Enhanced amount 37,100/-
20.

Accordingly, my answer to the above point is partly in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following;
ORDER 1) The appeal is allowed in part.
2) The impugned judgment and award dated 08.04.2010 passed in MVC.No.1386/2007 by the Fast Track IV & M.A.C.T., Belgaum is modified.

3) Amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal to the claimant is enhanced to Rs.1,06,600/-
as against Rs.69,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
4) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are held liable to pay the compensation.
5) Apportionment of amount is as per the order of the Tribunal.
6) On deposit, entire compensation amount is ordered to be released in favour of the claimant on due identification.
- 10 - Office to draw the award accordingly.
Amount in deposit, if any, is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of this judgment and award.

SD/-
